points.point: Guidance: hike expected once labor market improves further and Fed is reasonably confident inflation returns to 2 percent
points.quote: it would be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it sees some further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective
paraphrases: Fed will hike once it sees further labor-market gains and is reasonably confident inflation returns to 2%.
Liftoff is conditioned on more job-market improvement and being reasonably confident inflation heads back to 2 percent.
FOMC reiterated it needs further labor gains and to be reasonably confident inflation returns to 2 percent before raising rates.
decoys: Fed said it would hike once GDP growth exceeded 4 percent.
Committee said it needed to see inflation exceed 3 percent before easing policy.

points.point: Hold was driven partly by global growth concerns tied to slower growth in China
points.quote: recent global and financial market developments might restrain economic activity somewhat as a result of the higher level of the dollar and possible effects of slower economic growth in China
paraphrases: The hold reflected concerns over slowing growth in China and abroad.
Officials cited slower Chinese and global growth as a reason to hold rates steady.
Concerns about a China-led global slowdown argued for waiting to hike.
decoys: The hold was driven mainly by concerns over a U.S. government shutdown.
Officials said domestic labor market weakness was the main reason to delay.

points.point: Hold was also driven by financial-market volatility during the intermeeting period
points.quote: domestic financial conditions tightened modestly as concerns about prospects for global economic growth, centered on China, prompted an increase in financial market volatility and a deterioration in risk sentiment during the intermeeting period
paraphrases: Rising financial-market volatility and a deterioration in risk sentiment also argued for holding rates steady.
Turbulence in financial markets during the intermeeting period was cited as a reason for the pause.
Elevated market volatility, alongside the China-driven growth concerns, supported keeping rates on hold.
decoys: Financial markets were calm and orderly during the intermeeting period.
The hold was driven mainly by concerns over a U.S. government shutdown.

points.point: Unemployment rate fell to 5.1 percent in August

points.point: Inflation continued to run below the 2 percent objective
points.quote: Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports
paraphrases: Inflation stayed below the Fed's 2% goal.
Inflation remained under the Committee's 2 percent objective.

points.point: The inflation shortfall was held down by declines in energy and import prices
points.quote: Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports
paraphrases: The shortfall was held down by declines in energy prices and import prices.

points.point: Odds of a September hike fell during the intermeeting period

points.point: The expected fed funds path shifted down amid market turbulence
points.quote: Tighter financial market conditions and greater volatility contributed to a reduction of the odds that market participants appeared to place on the first increase in the federal funds rate occurring at the September FOMC meeting and to a flatter expected path for the policy rate thereafter.
